messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - SEV2: elevated streaming tail (p99) and streaming stalls across multi-region egress (eu-west / us-east). SLO p99 > 3s for streaming tail, p95 elevated. Auto-pager -> SRE team. Incident page: https://redwood.ops/incidents/5487654321 :rotating_light:

maria: acked. i'm on team for this one, pulling dashboards now. see pups in egress metrics.

sam: oncall here — thanks. pinging runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/streaming-tail. starting metric checks (p95/p99, streaming stalls by region).

raj: seeing spike in TLS handshake times on NAT egress nodes in eu-west-2. lots of retransmits and timeouts during TLS ClientHello. snippet from tcpdump on nat-azb-1:
```
15:42:12.123456 IP client->nat 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
15:42:12.223567 IP nat->client 443: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 29200, length 0
15:42:15.987654 IP client->nat 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmission)
15:42:18.000111 IP client->nat 443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0 (retransmission)
```
This lines up with TLS negotiate latencies ~2-6s on affected flows.

kevin: also seeing DNS SERVFAIL spikes for some egress subnets around same time window (eu-west-2). dig against our resolver shows repeated timeouts. could be partial resolver overload or blackholed traffic.

infra-sre: telemetry -> NAT SNAT port exhaustion pattern on natpool-eu-west-2-a: ephemeral-ports in use ~92%. lots of TIME_WAIT entries on proxy processes. netstat check: `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` -> 128k.

maria: good catch. possible root: hairpin/asymmetric egress causing retransmits + resolver timeouts. proposed mitigations: 1) steer streaming egress away from natpool-eu-west-2-a to natpool-eu-west-2-b, 2) temporarily expand ephemeral range on affected NAT proxies, 3) enable TCP keepalive on streaming frontends to reduce short-lived conn churn.

sam: applying steer now for streaming route table (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%). command: `redwoodctl egress steer apply --from natpool-eu-west-2-a --to natpool-eu-west-2-b --traffic-filter streaming --percentage 10`

maria: noted. i'll watch p99 and streaming stall graphs. cc @support-bot to surface customer impact.

sam: 10% applied -> monitoring. initial diff: p99 from 3.2s -> 2.1s on canary subset. leaving canary increasing.

support-bot: AUTOMATED CUSTOMER IMPACT: ~18% of streaming sessions in eu-west-2 experiencing stalls/error bursts. Top affected customers: cust-psi, cust-zen (sample request ids: req_0f3a, req_7b2c). Support tickets auto-created: #INC-548765-1, #INC-548765-2

raj: while canary ramping, i pushed a quick ephemeral port-range bump on nat-proxy nodes in eu-west-2-a (no-reboot):
```
echo 'net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 10240 65535' > /etc/sysctl.d/90-snat.conf
sysctl --system
```
This increases available SNAT ports. patch applied to pool nodes.

kevin: DNS errors decreased after steer and port bump, but still seeing isolated TLS stalls for long-lived streams (>60s). hypothesis: upstream keepalive idle timeouts terminating mid-stream causing reconnects. we should enable longer keepalive or allow session resumption.

maria: agree. temporary change: increase keepalive on streaming frontends: `proxy.conf: tcp_keepalive_time=120` pushed to staging then prod. also enabling session-resumption cache to reuse TLS sessions.

sam: keepalive + TLS session cache rolled to 30% -> monitoring. p99 now ~680ms, p95 ~170ms for streaming tail in eu-west-2 on metrics.

maria: customer impact update: support team notified, status page updated: "Partial streaming degradation in EU regions; mitigation in progress". CSMs engaged for top-tier customers.

infra-sre: note config diff for postmortem: possible proxypool autoscale mis-scaling combined with route-table change earlier today that increased cross-az hairpin. Need to capture control-plane route diffs.

support-bot: Customer-facing errors dropped to 4% affected after mitigations (was 18%). continuing watch.

kevin: plan for remainder: 1) keep current steer in place for 2 hours, 2) follow up with full NAT pool scale & autoscale tuning, 3) postmortem owner kevin, 4) action item to audit DNS resolver placement and retry/backoff config.

maria: handoff: i'll leave open until next oncall (5487658000). short summary for handoff notes:
- Incident 5487654321: multi-region streaming tail spike due to TLS handshake retransmits + SNAT exhaustion and DNS timeouts causing streaming stalls.
- Mitigations: egress steer to natpool-eu-west-2-b, expanded SNAT port range on nat-proxies, increased tcp_keepalive and enabled TLS session cache for streaming frontends.
- Current status: p99/p95 back within thresholds on affected traffic subsets, residual long-lived stream stalls reduced to low single-digit percent.
- Follow-ups: postmortem (owner: kevin), autoscale/tuning action for nat pools, route-table audit, customer outreach for cust-psi and cust-zen.

sam: leaving incident open for validation window. if stable for 2h, we'll move to sev3 and schedule postmortem. thx all. :thumbsup:

raj: +1, adding logs and tcpdump captures to incident page. will attach `pcap` snippets and timing histograms.

kevin: creating postmortem doc and timeline. assigning action items in playbook.

maria: handing off to night oncall, watch window set. oncall-bot will auto-escalate if p99 > 1s for 10m.

oncall-bot: NOTE: handoff scheduled to next oncall at 5487658000. reminders: run runbook step "egress-verify" and attach screenshots.

support-bot: final automated update: ETA for next update 15m. impacted sessions reduced.

sam: sg, closing realtime coordination. postmortem to follow.
